title: Automated Legal Deposition Indexing
business: Legal transcription firms managing high volumes of multi-party courtroom or deposition audio.
problem: Manual review of multi-hour audio files to identify who spoke and when is prohibitively expensive and prone to human error, leading to delays in producing searchable legal transcripts.
solution: The pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 pipeline automates the segmentation and speaker assignment process. By ingesting raw audio, it produces precise timestamps for each speaker, allowing downstream transcription services to align text with specific individuals automatically.
steps: Authenticate with Hugging Face to accept model conditions and generate an access token.
Install the pyannote.audio library and initialize the pipeline using the community-1 model identifier.
Load the audio file into the pipeline, optionally using a GPU for faster inference on long recordings.
Extract the speaker diarization output to generate a structured timeline of speaker segments.
Reconcile the diarization timestamps with text-based transcription outputs for final document generation.
outcome: A structured, searchable transcript where every block of text is accurately mapped to a specific speaker, significantly reducing the time required for manual verification.
limitation: The model assumes a mono input format; while it automatically downmixes multi-channel audio, this process may lose spatial information that could otherwise assist in distinguishing speakers in complex acoustic environments. Users should verify diarization accuracy when dealing with high-noise or overlapping speech scenarios.

diagram.description: The flow from raw audio input to a structured, searchable transcript.

code.content:
from pyannote.audio import Pipeline
# Initialize pipeline with token
pipeline = Pipeline.from_pretrained("pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1", token="{token}")
# Process audio file
output = pipeline("deposition_audio.wav")
# Iterate through segments to map speakers
for turn, speaker in output.speaker_diarization:
    print(f"{speaker} speaks between t={turn.start:.3f}s and t={turn.end:.3f}s")
